system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. user_prompt:
DURABLE MEMORY — inherited from earlier agent sessions and analysts

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived
    Enterprise prospects convert better through sales-assisted flows; the demo-request path outperformed self-serve on pipeline quality.

  memory_73 · consolidated day 31 · source archived
    SMB 40% discounts lifted acquisition and near-term revenue but cut retention 12%. Measured over four weeks in the standard SMB segment.

  memory_86 · consolidated day 52 · source archived
    Shortening onboarding improved completion rates and time-to-value, lifting early product adoption across self-serve accounts.

  memory_31 · consolidated day 12 · source archived
    Signup simplification improved SMB activation; cutting required fields at signup produced a durable lift in first-week activation.

  memory_91 · consolidated day 61 · source archived
    Activation messaging inside the product improved week-one engagement and nudged more accounts to their first meaningful action.

  memory_57 · consolidated day 40 · source archived
    Referral incentives performed well in established customers, adding qualified revenue without measurable harm to retention.

CURRENT SITUATION — day 76

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter
    · onboarding completion is down 4% quarter over quarter

  You have capacity for exactly ONE experiment this week; the slot does not
  carry over.

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:
    simplify_onboarding · promotional_pricing · referral_incentive ·
    activation_messaging · enterprise_sales_assist

Name the memories you want verified (up to 2, or none) and state the
action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale:
The two symptoms with hard numbers (activation -6% QoQ, onboarding completion -4% QoQ) both sit in the self-serve funnel, and the two inherited memories that speak directly to that funnel (memory_86 on shortened onboarding, memory_31 on signup field reduction) are the ones I would be leaning on hardest, so those are the two I spend verification budget on. I want the original records because both are consolidated summaries: I need the actual effect sizes, the measurement window, whether 'durable lift' in memory_31 was tracked past week one, and whether the memory_86 completion lift ever translated into retained revenue rather than just faster time-to-value. If either turns out to be a short-window read or measured under materially different funnel conditions than day 76, I would downgrade to activation_messaging (memory_91) as the cheaper adjacent test.

I am explicitly declining promotional_pricing despite the competitor pressure being the most urgent-feeling item. memory_73 records that 40% SMB discounts bought acquisition and near-term revenue at a 12% retention cost, measured over only four weeks — and a four-week window almost certainly understates the retention damage rather than overstating it. Against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, that is the direction most likely to book a win this quarter and destroy value later. Matching a competitor's entry price also tends to reset price expectations in a way that is hard to walk back.

Downstream value risk on my own chosen action: simplifying signup means cutting required fields, and memory_44 says enterprise converts better through sales-assisted demo-request flows. Fields removed at signup are often exactly the firmographic signals that route prospects into that path. So the experiment must be scoped to the SMB self-serve funnel and must not strip qualification data from the enterprise entry point, or I trade a measurable SMB activation lift for an unmeasured pipeline-quality loss. I will instrument enterprise demo-request volume and lead quality as a guardrail metric, not just activation.

Standard experiment rather than broad rollout: the inherited evidence is 15-64 days old, it predates both the competitor's move and the current funnel degradation, and I do not yet know whether the QoQ declines share a cause with what these experiments originally measured. A controlled test tells me whether the old finding still holds under current conditions; a broad rollout would assume it does. If verification comes back weak on both, I treat the inherited memories as stale rather than wrong and pick the lower-commitment activation_messaging test.
